transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Naomi Park (CTO, Mosaic Cloud), Luis Ortega (Platform Engineer), Erin Zhao (Security)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to validate integration surfaces for Redwood hosted/dedicated/private options; discuss SDKs & LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations, onramp gateway/edge proxy patterns, per-tenant quotas and rate-limits, and observability hooks for Mosaic's telemetry stack. Agree to POC and exchange docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, Alex from Redwood — thanks for blocking time. Uh, I'm joined by Marcus who will jump into the technical bits. Naomi, want to kick off with a quick context of what Mosaic is trying to solve?

[00:18] Naomi Park: Yeah, thanks Alex. We're building a multi-tenant recommendation and search platform for B2B e-commerce. Our current pipeline calls a mix of internal transformer services and a few managed LLM endpoints. The ask right now is twofold: one, unify model routing and cost controls; two, have a predictable SLA for our highest-value customers. We're evaluating hosted vs reserved/dedicated vs a private deployment that lives in our VPC.

[00:40] Marcus Lee: Cool. Quick clarifying q — when you say "unify model routing" do you mean per-tenant routing to different model sizes and also fallbacks for cost-sensitive tiers?

[00:48] Luis Ortega: Exactly. We want to route high-tier tenants to higher perf models with lower latency, but for internal cost controls have an automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants. And we want that routing to be enforced at the gateway level, ideally.

[01:05] Alex Chen: Got it. That maps to Redwood's smart routing and policy layer — we let you define per-tenant policies, can route by latency or cost, and have automatic fallback to compatible model variants. So integration surfaces are: SDK (server side), gateway/proxy pattern for edge routing, and some observability hooks.

[01:28] Naomi Park: On the SDK front: we already use LangChain in some pilots and have a few LamaIndex—sorry, LlamaIndex indexers. We need code samples that show how to hook Redwood into LangChain agents and also how to do streaming responses with our websocket layer.

[01:44] Marcus Lee: Totally. We have an SDK with a LangChain connector and a LlamaIndex adapter; I'll share the repo link. There are a few gotchas: the LangChain agent uses async streaming APIs so you'll want to use our streaming client to pipe tokens through your websocket. Also note that some of the older LlamaIndex integrations expect a blocking call, we have a small shim for that.

[02:08] Erin Zhao: Quick security note — we need to validate KMS integrations, key access patterns, and how audit logs are surfaced. On private deploys, we need an HSM or customer-managed KMS option, and end-to-end logging for compliance.

[02:23] Alex Chen: Understood. We support KMS integrations and can integrate with your cloud KMS or on-prem HSM depending on private install. Audit logs are available from the control plane, and for private we provide a control-plane forwarder and the raw audit stream. We'll include SOC 2 and ISO docs in the pack.

[02:40] Luis Ortega: On quotas — we need both rate limits and token quotas enforced per-tenant and per-route. Ideally something that lets us set daily token budgets and soft limits with alerts, and hard limits to prevent overages. Can Redwood's gateway enforce that, or do we need our own sidecar?

[02:58] Marcus Lee: You can do both. Redwood's hosted API supports per-api-key quotas and token-based billing; for dedicated or private you can run the Redwood gateway in a sidecar or edge proxy which enforces per-tenant rate limits, per-route quotas, and block/redirect policies. We also support sending webhooks/metrics when a quota is close to being hit so your billing and alerting systems can react.

[03:19] Naomi Park: So for the POC we'd like to test a sidecar pattern at our edge — minimal changes to our runtime, but consistent enforcement. Also we'd like to see token-level latency breakdowns so we can profile where time is being spent: network vs server vs KV cache.

[03:35] Marcus Lee: We can emit token-level traces and per-token latency metrics; they can be routed to Datadog/New Relic or a raw telemetry sink. Caveat: sampling rate matters for cost and volume — at high TPS you might choose 1% sampling.

[03:50] Naomi Park: That sounds fine. Another question — model quantization profiles. We plan to run smaller quantized models for low-tier tenants. Does Redwood automatically handle quantization compatibility and kernel selection for different hardware?

[04:05] Alex Chen: Yes, our runtime selects quantization-friendly execution paths and optimized kernels at runtime. For Dedicated you can pin a quantization profile per pool. For Hosted we have pre-configured variants and we can suggest profiles based on your sequence length distribution. We'll run a short profiling job during the POC to recommend settings.

[04:25] Luis Ortega: Excellent. On pricing — we need both per-token and per-hour estimates for a dedicated pool. Can you share a sample pricing spreadsheet?

[04:33] Alex Chen: Yep — I'll send a spreadsheet that shows hosted per-token rates, plus sample dedicated pool pricing (monthly commit and burst). Also what typical throughput looks like per GPU type.

[04:44] Erin Zhao: From a compliance standpoint, for private deployment we need SSO/SAML for admin access, RBAC, and the ability to retain logs for seven years. Can Redwood support long-term log retention, or do we need to ship logs into our SIEM?

[05:00] Marcus Lee: For Private we can keep logs in-place or forward to your SIEM. Long-term retention is usually handled by forwarding to your storage; control-plane logs can be exported. We'll detail the retention flow in the docs.

[05:12] Naomi Park: On latency SLOs: high-tier tenants require p95 < 120ms for generation up to 256 tokens. That seems aggressive. What's realistic?

[05:22] Marcus Lee: For short sequences on high-perf GPUs we can hit that on Dedicated if you provision for low contention and use batching strategies tuned for latency (small batch sizes, priority lanes). Hosted is possible but depends on multi-tenant noisy neighbors — Dedicated gives the predictability. We usually recommend dedicated pools for strict p95 latency SLOs.

[05:41] Naomi Park: Understood. Let's talk about integration effort — we have a microservices stack on k8s, and we already run an Envoy-based edge. How invasive is adding a Redwood sidecar or proxy?

[05:53] Alex Chen: The sidecar is a small container that intercepts model calls or forwards selected routes. We can provide an Envoy filter config as an example. It typically takes a few tickets to instrument: annotate pods, deploy sidecar, add routing rules. For LangChain/LlamaIndex in app code, integrating the SDK is often just swapping the client and providing the API key/tenant header.

[06:12] Luis Ortega: That Envoy plugin example will be huge. Also interested in canary rollouts — we want to test a model change for a single tenant before rolling org-wide.

[06:20] Marcus Lee: We support canary deploys and A/B routing — you can pin a tenant to a variant, do percentage rollouts, and set automatic fallback. Observability hooks will show any regressions by prompt set.

[06:33] Naomi Park: I keep hearing "prompt sets" — we want automatic quality regression alerts based on our tests. Is that part of Redwood Optimize or something custom?

[06:42] Alex Chen: That's Redwood Optimize territory — you can tie prompt sets/evals to monitors. If a metric drops (e.g., hallucination rate, end-to-end accuracy), we alert and can auto-fallback to a previous model. For the POC we can demonstrate a simple prompt-set eval pipeline.

[06:58] Erin Zhao: A small nit — can you clarify how identity is propagated? We need tenant ID in audit logs and in the control plane so that usage maps to customers for billing.

[07:08] Marcus Lee: We accept a tenant header (x-tenant-id) and map API keys to tenants. That same metadata gets attached to traces and billing. For private installs we can also do direct LDAP/SSO mapping for admin actions.

[07:20] Naomi Park: What about rate limiting between tenants if one goes rogue and floods the system? We want per-tenant hard limits plus the ability to throttle gracefully.

[07:29] Marcus Lee: You can do per-tenant token hard caps and soft caps. Soft caps emit webhooks and metrics, hard caps return a 429. With gateway sidecar you can implement graceful queueing or rejection logic client-side.

[07:42] Luis Ortega: For the POC, we'd like Redwood to run a simulated load test with our traffic pattern, and show both latency and cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated. Is that an ask you can take?

[07:52] Alex Chen: Yes — we'll need your sample traffic profile, desired SLOs, and tenant mapping. Marcus, we should plan a POC test harness and provide a recommended GPU config.

[08:03] Marcus Lee: I'll own the harness. For the test I've got a couple of templates: bursty e-commerce traffic and steady low-latency queries. We'll run both.

[08:13] Naomi Park: Great. A couple of smaller items — do you support streaming with tool-calling and structured outputs? We have downstream processors that expect JSON responses.

[08:23] Marcus Lee: We support streaming with function/tool calling and structured outputs. The SDK has a structured output helper to validate JSON schemas as tokens stream. There's a retry/fallback pattern if schema validation fails.

[08:36] Naomi Park: Lovely. Anything else we should cover?

[08:40] Alex Chen: One last practical note: for the POC we can give temporary trial keys with tenant-scoped quotas so you don't hit production limits. We'll also include a short quickstart showing LangChain and LlamaIndex usage, an Envoy filter example for the sidecar, and a sample observability dashboard JSON for Datadog.

[08:58] Erin Zhao: On compliance paperwork, we'll send over the standard vendor questionnaire. Expect questions about data deletion, encryption at rest and in transit, and who has access to keys.

[09:10] Alex Chen: We'll get that to you.

[09:13] Naomi Park: Recap then — Redwood to send pricing + SLA docs, SOC2/ISO/compliance pack, SDK examples for LangChain/LlamaIndex + Envoy sidecar sample, schedule POC week of 8/31, run load tests and provide latency/cost comparison. Customer to share traffic profile, tenant map, compliance questionnaire, and KMS requirements.

[09:34] Alex Chen: Exactly. Marcus and I will follow up with links and set a 2-hour POC slot. Any blockers on your side?

[09:41] Luis Ortega: No blockers. We might need legal to sign an NDA for deeper telemetry sharing but that's standard.

[09:47] Erin Zhao: We'll loop in legal and security reviewers; expect a 3–5 day turnaround.

[09:53] Alex Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the package by Monday.

[09:58] Naomi Park: Thanks all, appreciate it.

[10:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard terms ("LamaIndex" for LlamaIndex, "KV cash" for KV cache), some speaker overlap; timestamps approximate.
